question.text: Which of the following is NOT a currently SEBI-recognised national-level commodity derivatives exchange in India?

explanation.text: The Logic: FMC (Forward Markets Commission) was the regulator of commodity derivatives markets, not an exchange. It was merged with SEBI in 2015. Per the current SEBI recognition list, national commodity-derivatives exchanges include MCX, NCDEX, NSE, and BSE; ICEX recognition has been withdrawn per current SEBI material, so ICEX is no longer a currently recognised commodity derivatives exchange. The Trap: The NISM X-A workbook (p.194) still lists MCX, NCDEX, ICEX, NSE, and BSE; using that older list, ICEX would appear correct. The current SEBI position excludes ICEX, so this item uses NSE in its place as a current option. Cross-Exam Context: Commodity derivatives market structure is tested in NISM XVI, VIII, and X-A; the current SEBI recognition list (and not the older workbook listing) should be used for any "currently recognised" question.
